plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant, profit-maximizing strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding below 3 risks losing when second-highest < 3 and forfeiting positive surplus; bidding above 3 risks winning and paying a second-highest price above 3, yielding negative profit. With one round and no informative history, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. If there’s a tie at 3, the winner is random; expected profit conditional on winning remains nonnegative since the price equals the second-highest bid ≤ 3. ]

In a 3-bidder independent private values second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. There’s no prior history to exploit, and others’ values are uniformly drawn and independent each round. By bidding my value ($35), I win exactly when my value is highest and pay the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Tie-breaking is random; bidding above or below my value can only reduce expected payoff. Therefore, bid exactly 35.

[ Second-price auction with three bidders and independent private values drawn uniformly 0–49. Dominant strategy is truthful bidding: bidding your exact value maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks negative payoff if I win and pay above my value; underbidding risks losing when paying less than value would still yield positive surplus. With no prior history to exploit in this single round, follow dominant strategy. My value is 11, so bid 11.0 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 11 and earn 11 − (second-highest bid). ]
